name: Argentine Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sign language. Grammars exist (Massone 1996 Gramatica y lexico de la lengua de senas Argentina; Massone & Machado 1994) but none reachable and word stress category inapplicable; no stress/prosody description found.

sources.citation: Martínez, Rocío Anabel. 2016. Reconsideración, desde un Enfoque Cognitivo-Prototípico, del adjetivo como clase de palabras en la Lengua de Señas Argentina (LSA). Tesis doctoral, Universidad de Buenos Aires.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only prosody remark (p. 161, PDF p. 162): eye contact C+/-, 'ciertos rasgos no manuales (RNM) y el uso distintivo del espacio conforman la prosodia de la LSA' (information-structure prosody). No word stress.

sources.citation: Massone, María Ignacia. 1996. Gramática y léxico de la lengua de señas Argentina. Tesis doctoral, Universidad de Buenos Aires, Facultad de Filosofía y Letras. 382 pp. (Glottolog ref 588448)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Ch. IV 'Sistema para la descripción fonética de la LSA' (pp. 72-110) is a Liddell-Johnson movement/hold transcription with temporal-quality features [lento]/[sost] and spatial-quality features [amp]/[meng]/[tns] ('tenso.. describe una D más fuerte', PDF p. 84 ≈ printed p. 82); initial holds may be lengthened 'para indicar intensidad, ej.: CARO, CARO[intens]'. No word-stress or accent description anywhere. In ch. sources.citation: Caceres, Roman. 2017. Lexical categories in Lengua de Señas Argentina. MA thesis, University of North Dakota (adv. Kathryn L. Hansen). xiv+223 pp. (Glottolog ref 579501)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syntactic study (constituency tests); phonology mentioned only as 'some aspects of LSA morphology and phonology have been considered to support the analysis' (p. 2); non-manuals treated only as syntactic-boundary markers (Principle #4). Silent on stress. downloaded from the the Internet Archive snapshot (2024-07-28) of commons.und.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=3104&context=theses because commons.und.edu is behind an automated-access block.

sources.citation: Manrique, Elizabeth. 2017. Achieving mutual understanding in Argentine Sign Language (LSA). PhD dissertation, Radboud University Nijmegen (MPI Series in Psycholinguistics 121). xviii+219 pp. (Glottolog ref 550577)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2.2.4 Phonology (pp. 29-33) describes the four parameters (handshape, location, movement, orientation) only. §2.2.6 (p. 35): 'NMMs are suprasegmental features in signed languages spreading over a group of signs, clause or utterance like intonation in spoken languages (Sandler, 2010)', with fn. 6 defining suprasegmental features generically as 'prosodic features in phonetics such as stress or tone'. No statement about word/sign stress in LSA.
